policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the qere first-person suffix: "for he hath told me all his heart" (li), not the ketiv lah "he had told her". The ASV note "Or, according to another reading, he had told her" is classed alternative_rendering and does not itself decide the unit, but the rendered text is unambiguously li.

Qere ha-asurim and ketiv ha-asirim are a purely orthographic plene/defective difference in the same noun; ASV "in the prison-house" renders beth ha-asurim either way, and no ASV note is mapped here. Base fallback carries the projection.

ASV's temporal construction "And it came to pass, when their hearts were merry, that they said" renders the qere infinitive ke-tov ("when [their heart] was merry"); the ketiv ki tov would give a causal "for their heart was merry", which the ASV does not render.

Qere ha-asurim and ketiv ha-asirim differ only in plene/defective spelling of the same noun; ASV "out of the prison-house" is compatible with both and no ASV note is mapped here. Base fallback carries the projection.

Qere va-hamisheni and ketiv ve-himsheni differ only in the written yod of the same verb form; ASV "Suffer me that I may feel the pillars" renders it identically either way, and no ASV note is mapped here. Base fallback carries the projection.
